title: Whose Wages Make It Into the Survey? — Reuben Gronau’s Reservation Wage Puzzle, James Heckman’s (1979) Two-Step Inverse Mills Ratio Selection Correction & Thomas Mroz’s PSID Married Women’s Labor-Supply Tests

teenKit.tldr: In 15 seconds: Surveys can only record hourly wages for people currently working—so estimating wage equations on workers alone hides everyone whose market offer fell below their home reservation wage. Heckman's (1979) selection correction turns missing nonworkers from a mystery into an omitted variable we can model.
teenKit.whyItMatters: From labor economics to clinical follow-up, analyzing only 'who showed up' confuses selection into the sample with real causal effects.
keyTakeaways: Reuben Gronau highlighted the reservation-wage threshold: we observe market wage W only when W exceeds an individual's reservation value of non-market time W*.
James Heckman (1979) proved truncation of the error term creates an omitted-variable bias proportional to the Inverse Mills Ratio lambda(Z*gamma) from a first-stage participation probit.

Thomas Mroz (1987) tested married women's labor supply in PSID microdata, demonstrating why credible exclusion restrictions (variables shifting participation without directly shifting wage offers) anchor selection models.

vocab.meaning: The minimum hourly wage offer required to induce a person to enter paid employment.
phi(z) / Phi(z)—standard normal density over cumulative probability, capturing expected truncated error given selection.
A variable affecting probability of sample participation (stage 1) without directly entering the outcome equation (stage 2).

quiz.question: Why does running ordinary least squares (OLS) only on employed respondents bias market-wage estimates?
options: Workers are non-randomly selected on having unobserved wage/participation shocks high enough to cross their reservation threshold
OLS cannot divide by hours worked
Census computers round wages to integers
quiz.explanation: Conditioning on employment truncates the joint error distribution, making E[u_i | working] nonzero and correlated with covariates.
